From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation scope, quickstart endpoints & rate check

Hi Kunal / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciate the candid product context. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a hosted eval that surfaces the right tradeoffs vs Dedicated/VPC for Payloom.

Key notes from the demo:
- Primary use: transactional receipt classification + summarization inside your payments flow (low latency, mix of short and medium prompts).
- Expected peak concurrency: ~120 qps for upstream validation service during batch settlement windows (spikes for ~10–12 minutes).
- Typical prompt size: 120–450 tokens; some long-form summarization jobs up to ~1.5k tokens but only ~2% of traffic.
- Data residency: US-only for now; standard SOC2 controls required.

Asks / next steps so we can produce a concrete hosted quickstart plan: 
1) Confirm target SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets we should plan for) and acceptable tail latency.
2) Which endpoints in your stack will call the API? Are you planning an async worker for long summaries or sync calls from the request path?
3) Any procurement timing or constraints (standard PO vs SOW vs platform purchase)?

What I’ll provide once we have the above: a short hosted quickstart playbook (sandbox endpoints, recommended rate caps & concurrency settings, KV/prefix cache suggestions, and a runway plan to evaluate Dedicated if you outgrow hosted economics). I’ll include a simple cost/runbook and a sample canary routing policy for safety.

I’ve tentatively scoped a hosted sandbox with three endpoints (chat-short, gen-medium, gen-long) and an initial rate slice that we can expand during the trial. If that fits, I’ll share the sandbox invite + a one-page runbook and get ops access turned on.

Would you be available for a 20-minute follow-up tomorrow to confirm SLOs and endpoint mapping?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0189

Thanks Jordan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SLOs: p50 <= 60ms for the short prompts, p95 <= 220ms for medium (we can tolerate up to 1.5s p95 for the rare long summaries).
- Call patterns: most validation calls are sync from the request path (~95% short prompts). Long summaries will be kicked to an async worker and pulled occasionally.
- Peak window: the 120 qps spike comes from a 10-minute settlement batch that occurs once every ~3 hours during business hours. Outside of that we expect ~12–15 qps sustained.
- Procurement: we do a standard PO for pilots under $50k; >$50k will need pre-approved SOW. I’ll loop procurement if/when we get to pricing.

Can you confirm safe default rate caps per endpoint for hosted sandbox and the canary fallback plan if we exceed capacity? Also need to confirm whether Redwood can provide logging of token-level latency for our SREs during the trial.

Thanks —

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Great context — here’s a pragmatic hosted quickstart configuration we can spin up today for Payloom: 

1) Endpoint mapping & initial rate slice
- chat-short (short validation prompts): allocate 25 qps slice; burst policy + autoscaling to 60 qps for the settlement window. Model: redwood-serve-14b-fp16 (low latency profile). Target p95 ~180ms with our network assumptions.
- gen-medium (mid-length summarization/response): allocate 8 qps slice; burst to 20 qps. Model: redwood-serve-13b-q4 (balanced perf/cost). Target p95 ~350–600ms.
- gen-long (long summaries async worker): background workers only, allocate 2 qps; default to async queue processing and allow up to 6 concurrent jobs. Model: redwood-long-quant (cost optimized).

2) Canary & oversubscription policy
- Canary policy: start 2% of traffic on a slightly larger instance profile; monitor p95 and token error rate for 30 minutes.
- Fallback policy: automatically reduce gen-medium token window to 75% of configured context length and route excess to gen-long async queue OR fall back to a lower-cost model variant (redwood-serve-13b-q8) for non-critical traffic.

3) Rate limiting & safety knobs
- Global trial quota: 150k tokens/day initial. Endpoint-level rate limiting via per-endpoint qps (enforced at gateway).
- Temporary soft-throttles: if p95 > target for 3 consecutive minutes, auto-engage soft-throttle and send 429s at 10% sample to protect critical paths and trigger alert to SREs.

4) Observability & logs
- We can stream token-level latency and request/response IDs to a customer-controlled CloudWatch / Datadog forwarder for the trial. We’ll provide a configurable retention window (30 days default).

5) Deliverables & timeline
- Today: create sandbox endpoints, seed quota, and send invite (1 business day).
- +1 business day after onboarding: run a 30-minute traffic rehearsal mimicking the settlement spike (we’ll coordinate a window).
- Week 1: provide latency/cost dashboard and canary readout; review Dedicated fit if sustained spikes push hosted cost over threshold.

I attached an updated quickstart playbook and the simple rate table for their procurement to review. I’ll also prepare a short SOW template in case procurement needs it for >$50k pilots.

If this looks good I’ll ask onboarding to provision the sandbox and send the invite to kunal@payloom.com + procurement.

—Ben
